paper_metadata.title: Prognosis of juvenile myoclonic epilepsy is related to endophenotypes

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study recruited consecutive patients from a specialized tertiary center with clear inclusion/exclusion criteria and a high participation rate (85.5%). Baseline characteristics are well-described.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: All patients were followed up in the outpatient clinic of a tertiary center (Epilepsy Section, Department of Neurology and Neurosurgery, Universidade Federal de São Paulo, São Paulo, Brazil).
items.reasoning: The setting and population (JME patients at a university hospital) are clearly defined.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: Consecutive patients who met clinical and EEG criteria for JME diagnosis were submitted to a video-EEG monitoring
items.reasoning: Consecutive recruitment in a clinical setting reduces selection bias compared to convenience sampling.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: Inclusion criteria were: (a) unequivocal diagnosis of JME based on criteria defined in the revised Classification of Epilepsies and Epileptic Syndromes; (b) age over 12 years; (c) no evidence of neurological or intellectual deficits and (d) more than 4 years of formal education.
items.reasoning: Criteria are specific and based on international classification standards.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: Prognostic factors (reflex traits) were measured using a standardized, objective video-EEG protocol based on established neuropsychological tasks.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: Reflex traits were defined as seizures and/or EEG discharges induction by eye-closure, photic stimulation, language, praxis or calculation.
items.reasoning: The prognostic factors are clearly defined and categorized.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: Video-EEG was recorded on a 32-channel digital equipment (Biologic1, software Ceegraph1) using the 10–20 International Electrode System... The protocol and its analysis were based on those reported by Matsuoka et al.7 and Mayer.22
items.reasoning: The use of digital video-EEG and established protocols ensures high reliability.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: Age at epilepsy onset (years) 13.70 ± 4.48; Duration of epilepsy (years) 10.73 ± 8.73
items.reasoning: Continuous variables like age and duration are reported with means and standard deviations.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: All patients had 30 min of awake EEG recording starting at 7 a.m. After this baseline record, patients performed habitual methods of activation
items.reasoning: A standardized protocol was applied to all participants.

items.label: Proportion of data on PF available for analysis
items.prompt: Adequate proportion of the study sample has complete data for PF variable.
items.evidence_snippet: Sixty-five consecutive JME patients had video-EEG recording
items.reasoning: All 65 patients included in the analysis underwent the PF measurement.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (seizure control) relied on patient/family recall and seizure calendars, which is standard but susceptible to recall bias. However, the criteria used (Prasad et al.) are validated.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: Evaluation of seizure control was done according to Prasad et al. [24]... Group 1: good seizure control for all seizure types in the last two years and Group 2: moderate or poor seizure control.
items.reasoning: The outcome is clearly defined using a validated scale and a specific timeframe (2 years).

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: Estimation of the frequency of seizures was based on the review of seizure calendars and specific questioning of the patient and family members.
items.reasoning: While standard in epilepsy research, self-reporting and calendars are less reliable than objective monitoring. No blinding of outcome assessors is mentioned.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: The various seizure types, possible seizure triggers, AED therapy, treatment adherence and adverse effects were observed as well as routine blood tests, AED level determination, and routine EEGs.
items.reasoning: All patients were followed in the same outpatient clinic with the same monitoring procedures.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: While many potential confounders (age, duration, psychiatric comorbidities, AED use) were measured and compared between groups, the study did not use multivariable analysis to adjust for these factors simultaneously.
